chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of Maghrib, and he said: “Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله for every salat (prayer) with two times, except the Maghrib salat (prayer), for indeed its time is one, and its time is its obligation.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: There is no contradiction between these two reports and what we have previously presented of reports stating that Maghrib has two times: its beginning is the setting of the sun, and its end is the disappearance of the twilight or the interlacing of the stars. This is because if a person prays at the time the redness disappears from the eastern side and proceeds deliberately in his salat (prayer), he will not finish an obligatory and supererogatory salat (prayer) except that the twilight will already have vanished and the stars will have appeared. What further clarifies what we have presented—that these two salats (prayers) have two times, and that what was negated by the two preceding reports was only the expansiveness of the time—is what he narrated:
(1037) 74 — Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, who said:

I wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: Our companions have mentioned that when the sun passes the meridian, the time of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr has entered, and when it sets, the time of Maghrib and the later ʿIshāʾ has entered, except that this one is before that one in travel and residence, and that the time of Maghrib extends to a quarter of the night. So he عليه السلام wrote: “That is how the time is, except that the time of Maghrib is narrow, and the end of its time is the disappearance of the redness and its turning into whiteness on the western horizon.”
(1038) 75 — Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān, who said:

I wrote to him: A man may be in a house whose walls prevent him from seeing the redness of the west and from knowing the disappearance of the twilight and the time of the later ʿIshāʾ salat (prayer). When should he perform it, and what should he do? So he عليه السلام wrote: “He should perform it, if he is in this condition, when the stars become apparent; and ʿIshāʾ at the time of their interlacing and the whitening of the place of the sun’s setting.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The meaning of ‘the shortening of the stars’ is their becoming apparent.

key_terms.اشْتِبَاكُ النُّجُومِ: the dense appearance or interlacing of the stars
key_terms.بَيَاضِ مَغِيبِ الشَّمْسِ: the whitening at the place of the sun’s setting
key_terms.ذَهَابُ الْحُمْرَةِ: the disappearance of the red twilight
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْمَغْرِبِ: the legally recognized time for the Maghrib salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timing of Maghrib salat (prayer) and explains that although some reports describe it as having a single immediate time of obligation, other reports establish a limited beginning and end for its valid period. The passage also clarifies practical signs for determining the end of Maghrib time and the onset of ʿIshāʾ, especially when direct observation of the horizon is obstructed.
